# Configuration

<!-- config-table:start – generated by "npm run config:docs" from server/src/config-schema.ts; do not edit by hand -->

Steward is configured with environment variables. All of them are checked when the server starts: an invalid value (a port that is not a number, an unknown mode, a limit out of range) refuses to start and names every bad variable on its own line, e.g.

```text
Invalid configuration – fix these environment variables and start again:
  SM_PORT: "80a" is not a whole number from 0 to 65535
  SM_API_DOCS: "everyone" is not one of off, authenticated, public
```

An empty value counts as not set. On/off variables accept `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off` and `yes`/`no`. Settings that can also be changed in the UI (under **Settings**) are noted; the variable then wins over the setting.

**Secrets from files.** Every secret variable can come from a file instead: set `<NAME>_FILE` to its path (`SM_DATABASE_URL_FILE`, `SM_SENTRY_DSN_FILE`, `SM_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE_FILE`, `SM_BACKUP_RESTORE_TEST_DATABASE_URL_FILE`, `SM_TRANSFER_PASSPHRASE_FILE`; the master passphrase has `SM_MASTER_PASSPHRASE_FILE`). The file holds the value, a trailing line break is ignored, and `%d/…` means the systemd credentials folder. Docker and Kubernetes secrets are files, and a file does not show up in `docker inspect`, `kubectl describe` or `/proc/<pid>/environ`. Setting both `<NAME>` and `<NAME>_FILE` refuses to start.

**Unknown variables.** At start-up Steward logs a warning for every `SM_…` variable it does not know, with the closest known name (`unknown environment variable SM_DATABSE_URL is ignored – did you mean SM_DATABASE_URL?`). It names the variable, never its value.

The tables are generated from `server/src/config-schema.ts` by `npm run config:docs` (CI checks them with `npm run config:docs -- --check`). Tests that change a variable while the server runs call `reloadConfig()` from `server/src/config.ts` (see [TESTING.md](TESTING.md)).

## Server and network

| Variable                        | Default         | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_PORT`                       | `4310`          | HTTP port (`0`: any free port, shown in the start log)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `SM_HOST`                       | `127.0.0.1`     | Bind address. Keep it local unless you know what you are doing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SM_ALLOWED_HOSTS`              | –               | Extra allowed `Host` headers (comma-separated), e.g. the machine's DNS name when colleagues use it                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `SM_TEAMS_BOT_PORT`             | –               | Port of a second, minimal listener for the Microsoft Teams bot (preview, ADR 0013): it serves only `POST /teams/bot/messages` – no cookies, no web app, no other route. Not set: no bot listener. Publish only this port to the internet (docs/TEAMS.md).                                                                       |
| `SM_TEAMS_BOT_HOST`             | –               | Bind address of the Teams bot listener (default: `SM_HOST`). Uses `SM_TLS_CERT`/`SM_TLS_KEY` like the main listener.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SM_TLS_CERT`                   | –               | Path to a certificate (PEM). With `SM_TLS_KEY` Steward serves HTTPS, which is recommended when others connect over the network.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SM_TLS_KEY`                    | –               | Path to the private key of `SM_TLS_CERT` (PEM)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SM_TLS_CIPHERS`                | modern list     | OpenSSL cipher list for TLS 1.2 with the built-in HTTPS (TLS 1.3 suites are always on; TLS 1.0/1.1 are off)                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `SM_PUBLIC_URL`                 | –               | External URL (e.g. `https://steward.corp.example`, or `https://apps.corp.example/steward`) behind a reverse proxy. Used for the SSO redirect URI and links; `https://` makes the session cookie `Secure` and turns on HSTS. Its path is the base path.                                                                          |
| `SM_BASE_PATH`                  | – (the root)    | Path prefix behind a reverse proxy, e.g. `/steward`: everything (UI, `/api`, health) moves below it; the proxy must not strip it. Must match the path of `SM_PUBLIC_URL`. An own subdomain is safer: [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md#behind-a-reverse-proxy)                                                                            |
| `SM_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`     | `25`            | On SIGTERM/SIGINT: how long running steps may still finish before their runs are marked interrupted. Give the container a little more (Docker `stop_grace_period`, Kubernetes `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`), see [docs/INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)                                                                               |
| `SM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`    | `120`           | How long a client may take to send a request (its body) before the connection is closed with 408 – a slow body cannot hold a connection open (0 = no limit). Downloads are not limited by it; signed-in uploads get `SM_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`                                                                                 |
| `SM_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`     | `3600`          | The same for uploads of signed-in users (files, migration packages, routes that accept more than 1 MB) – raise it for very large migration packages over slow links (0 = no limit)                                                                                                                                              |
| `SM_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `600`           | A connection on which nothing is sent or received for this long is closed (0 = never); a running download keeps it busy                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `SM_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `72`            | How long an idle keep-alive connection stays open after a response. Behind a load balancer keep it above the balancer’s idle timeout                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SM_TRUST_PROXY`                | – (off)         | Behind a reverse proxy: the proxies' addresses/CIDRs (`10.0.0.5,10.1.0.0/16`, `loopback`) or the number of proxies (`1`, only for a proxy on a loopback/private address) whose `X-Forwarded-For/-Proto/-Host` are believed. Client addresses in the audit log, sign-in lockouts and webhook CIDR checks then are the real ones. |
| `SM_OUTBOUND_POLICY`            | – (the setting) | Where platform calls, notifications and webhooks may connect: `platforms`, `allowList` or `open`. Overrides **Settings → Outbound connections**; loopback, link-local addresses and the own port are always blocked.                                                                                                            |
| `HTTPS_PROXY`                   | –               | Corporate proxy (also `HTTP_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`), used for platform calls unless a platform overrides it                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `SM_DEMO`                       | `off`           | `1` mounts the mock platforms under `/mock` and offers the demo data                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Database and data

| Variable                            | Default                          | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_DATASET_CACHE_ROWS`             | `100000`                         | Parsed dataset rows kept in memory between reads (dashboards, API pages); `0` turns the cache off                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SM_DATA_DIR`                       | `./data`                         | Data directory                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `SM_DATABASE_URL`                   | – (SQLite in the data directory) | Use PostgreSQL: `postgres://user:password@host:5432/database`. Not available in the desktop executable. See [Database](INSTALL.md#5-database-sqlite-or-postgresql). Or `SM_DATABASE_URL_FILE`: a file with the URL (a Docker or Kubernetes secret)                                |
| `SM_DATABASE_SCHEMA`                | `public`                         | PostgreSQL schema (created if missing)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SM_DATABASE_CA`                    | –                                | CA certificate (PEM file) for verifying the PostgreSQL server's TLS certificate                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `SM_UPGRADE_BACKUPS`                | `3`                              | Automatic copies of the database made before an update migrates it, kept in `SM_UPGRADE_BACKUP_DIR` (`0` = none): a SQLite copy, or a `pg_dump` of the PostgreSQL schema (`SM_PG_DUMP`). See [Updating](INSTALL.md#6-updating)                                                    |
| `SM_UPGRADE_BACKUP_DIR`             | `<data dir>/backups`             | Folder of the automatic copies made before an update migrates the database (e.g. another volume for a large PostgreSQL dump)                                                                                                                                                      |
| `SM_UPGRADE_BACKUP_REQUIRED`        | `on`                             | When the copy before migrating fails (no disk space, no `pg_dump`, a `pg_dump` older than the PostgreSQL server), the start stops without changing the database. `0` logs a warning and migrates without the copy                                                                 |
| `SM_UPGRADE_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `3600`                           | PostgreSQL: longest time the `pg_dump` before migrating may take (`0` = no limit); a dump that takes longer counts as failed                                                                                                                                                      |
| `SM_DB_SLOW_MS`                     | `200`                            | Statements and transactions that take longer are logged as `slow database statement` (start of the SQL, no values; at most once a minute each) and counted in `sm_db_slow_statements_total` (`0` = off). See [docs/METRICS.md](METRICS.md#database)                               |
| `SM_SQLITE_AUTO_VACUUM`             | `on`                             | SQLite: new databases are created with incremental auto-vacuum, and the retention clean-up gives deleted space back to the file system in small steps. `0`: new databases without it                                                                                              |
| `SM_SQLITE_VACUUM_AT_START`         | `off`                            | SQLite: `1` rewrites the database file before the server starts (VACUUM; seconds per GB, nothing answers meanwhile) and turns on incremental auto-vacuum – once, for a database made before 0.11 after a large clean-up. See [Disk space](INSTALL.md#disk-space-after-a-clean-up) |
| `SM_METRIC_RETENTION_DAYS`          | `400`                            | How long dashboard metric history is kept                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `SM_AI_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS`        | `400`                            | How long the usage log of AI model calls is kept (days; budgets need the current month). See [AI models](AI.md#reporting)                                                                                                                                                         |

## Unlocking

| Variable                    | Default | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_MASTER_PASSPHRASE_FILE` | –       | File with the master passphrase: unlock automatically at start-up, so schedules run after a reboot. Use a Docker secret, a systemd credential (`%d/…`) or a file only the service account can read. |
| `SM_MASTER_PASSPHRASE`      | –       | The same, as a variable (prefer the file). Both are removed from the environment at start, so child processes never see them.                                                                       |

## Sign-in and sessions

| Variable                       | Default         | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SM_PASSWORD_LOGIN`            | – (the setting) | Who may sign in with a password: `all`, `adminsOnly` or `none` (single sign-on only, from an admin's first SSO). Wins over **Settings → Sign-in**, which then shows it read-only. Emergency access from the server's command line works in every mode ([docs/INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md#locked-out-of-single-sign-on)).                                    |
| `SM_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES`      | `30`            | A session ends after this many minutes without a request (an open Steward tab keeps it alive), 5–10080                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SM_SESSION_MAX_HOURS`         | `12`            | A session ends this many hours after sign-in, used or not (OWASP ASVS level 2), 1–720                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SM_STEP_UP_MINUTES`           | `5`             | How long a confirmation for sensitive actions lasts (step-up: the password again or a fresh single sign-on), 1–15; also the oldest `auth_time` accepted. The longest age: the assurance policy can set a shorter one per action ([docs/ASSURANCE.md](ASSURANCE.md)). See [docs/SECURITY-HARDENING.md](SECURITY-HARDENING.md#step-up-re-authentication) |
| `SM_PASSWORD_HASH_CONCURRENCY` | `2`             | Password hashes computed at the same time; further sign-ins wait in a short queue (503 when it is full)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Limits

| Variable                   | Default   | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `600`     | Requests per minute and signed-in user (otherwise per client address) on the web app's API, webhooks and web UI files; expensive actions have lower limits of their own; `0` = off. See [docs/SECURITY-HARDENING.md](SECURITY-HARDENING.md#request-rate-limits) |
| `SM_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS`   | `20`      | Runs at the same time; more wait in status _queued_ (first come, first served) until one ends or waits for a decision. `0`: no limit                                                                                                                            |
| `SM_MAP_CACHE_MB`          | `256`     | Disk cache of the map of sites (`<data>/cache/map/`, least recently used out), in MB; `0` = no disk cache. See [docs/PLANT.md](PLANT.md#map)                                                                                                                    |
| `SM_EVENT_LOOP_WARN_MS`    | `1000`    | A warning is logged when the event loop was blocked longer (at most once a minute); `sm_event_loop_lag_seconds` has the p99                                                                                                                                     |
| `SM_EXPR_TIMEOUT_MS`       | `5000`    | Time limit of one JSONata expression evaluation (ms)                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SM_EXPR_MAX_DEPTH`        | `1000`    | Maximum recursion depth of a JSONata expression                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SM_EXPR_MAX_SEQUENCE`     | `1000000` | Longest sequence (array, range `[a..b]`) a JSONata expression may create                                                                                                                                                                                        |

## API, MCP and metrics

| Variable                     | Default         | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_API_V1`                  | `on`            | `off` turns the public REST API (`/api/v1`) and its documentation off                                                                                                                                      |
| `SM_API_DOCS`                | – (the setting) | Who may open the API documentation (`/api/docs/`, `openapi.json` without a token): `off`, `authenticated` (signed-in users, the default) or `public`. Overrides the setting under **Settings → REST API**. |
| `SM_API_RATE_LIMIT`          | `600`           | Requests per minute and API token on `/api/v1`; `0` = unlimited                                                                                                                                            |
| `SM_MCP`                     | – (the setting) | `off` turns the MCP server (`/api/mcp`) off, whatever **Settings → MCP server** says (`on` has no effect: the setting decides)                                                                             |
| `SM_MCP_RATE_LIMIT`          | `120`           | MCP requests per minute and token                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `SM_MCP_GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT`  | `30`            | MCP platform gateway calls per minute, user and platform                                                                                                                                                   |
| `SM_MCP_GATEWAY_CONCURRENCY` | `2`             | MCP gateway calls at the same time per platform (never more than half of the platform's _max. concurrent requests_)                                                                                        |
| `SM_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`     | –               | Origins of browser-based MCP clients allowed to call `/api/mcp` (comma-separated)                                                                                                                          |
| `SM_METRICS_PUBLIC`          | `off`           | `1` serves `/api/metrics` without sign-in (otherwise admins, auditors or an API token)                                                                                                                     |

## Audit log and evidence

| Variable                      | Default | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_AUDIT_ANCHOR`             | –       | A signed audit checkpoint kept outside Steward. Every verification fails if the log is shorter than it or differs. See [docs/SECURITY-HARDENING.md](SECURITY-HARDENING.md#audit-log-as-evidence). |
| `SM_AUDIT_ANCHOR_FILE`        | –       | A file with a signed audit checkpoint (e.g. on a write-once share); checked like `SM_AUDIT_ANCHOR`                                                                                                |
| `SM_AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_MINUTES` | `60`    | Interval of signed audit checkpoints (at least 5)                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SM_AUDIT_FULL_VERIFY_DAYS`   | `7`     | Days between automatic full verifications of the audit chain in the background (`0`: only by hand). _Verify chain_ itself is incremental, from the newest signed checkpoint                       |
| `SM_EVIDENCE_MAX_MB`          | `512`   | Largest audit evidence pack (MB)                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SM_EVIDENCE_RETENTION_DAYS`  | `7`     | How long a built evidence pack is kept for download                                                                                                                                               |

## Browser steps and reports

| Variable              | Default | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_CHROMIUM_SANDBOX` | `auto`  | `1`/`0` forces Chromium's sandbox for browser steps on/off (default: on, except as root)                                                                                                          |
| `SM_CHROMIUM_PATH`    | –       | Use a specific Chromium/Chrome binary for browser steps                                                                                                                                           |
| `SM_PDF_WORKER`       | `auto`  | PDF reports are drawn in a worker thread (`auto`; falls back to the main thread when it cannot start) or always in the main thread (`off`, no time limit then). See [docs/REPORTS.md](REPORTS.md) |

## Logging, tracing and error reporting

| Variable                             | Default             | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_LOG_LEVEL`                       | `info`              | `fatal`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace` or `silent`. Logs are JSON lines on stdout.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `SM_LOG_LEVEL_FORMAT`                | `number`            | How log lines carry their level: `number` (pino: `"level":30`) or `label` (`"level":"info"`, for Loki, Elasticsearch or Cloud Logging pipelines that expect words)                                                                                         |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`        | –                   | Turns on OpenTelemetry tracing (OTLP/HTTP). Standard `OTEL_*` variables apply, e.g. `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`.                                                                                                                  |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` | –                   | The traces endpoint only (wins over `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`)                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`                  | `steward`           | Service name of the traces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SM_OTEL_PROPAGATE`                  | `on`                | `0` stops adding `traceparent` headers to platform calls                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `SM_SENTRY_DSN`                      | –                   | Report unexpected errors to Sentry, GlitchTip or Bugsink (off by default; scrubbed, no personal data). More variables and exactly what is sent: [docs/ERROR-REPORTING.md](ERROR-REPORTING.md). An invalid DSN only logs a warning. Or `SM_SENTRY_DSN_FILE` |
| `SM_SENTRY_DSN_WEB`                  | `SM_SENTRY_DSN`     | DSN for errors in the web UI (`off` turns browser reporting off)                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `SM_SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`              | `production`        | Environment name of reported errors                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SM_SENTRY_RELEASE`                  | `steward@<version>` | Release name of reported errors                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SM_SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE`       | `0`                 | Share of requests traced to Sentry, 0–1 (0 = errors only); ignored while OpenTelemetry export is on                                                                                                                                                        |

## Backups and migration

| Variable                              | Default      | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SM_PG_DUMP`                          | `pg_dump`    | `pg_dump` program for backups of a PostgreSQL database (a newer server needs a matching version)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `SM_PG_RESTORE`                       | `pg_restore` | `pg_restore` program for restores                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SM_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE`                | –            | Passphrase for `steward backup` (automation only; prefer `--passphrase-file` or the prompt). Or `SM_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE_FILE`                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `SM_BACKUP_RESTORE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | –            | PostgreSQL: a database of its own (not the live one) the weekly restore test restores the newest backup into, to check its tables and audit chain, then drops it again. Without it the test only reads the dump (`pg_restore --list`). Or `SM_BACKUP_RESTORE_TEST_DATABASE_URL_FILE`. See [docs/BACKUPS.md](BACKUPS.md#the-restore-test) |
| `SM_BACKUP_SINGLE_PUT_BYTES`          | `33554432`   | S3 backups: larger archives are uploaded in parts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SM_BACKUP_PART_BYTES`                | `16777216`   | S3 backups: size of one part of a multipart upload (larger for archives that would need more than 10,000 parts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `SM_MIGRATION_MAX_MB`                 | `2048`       | Largest migration package the web UI accepts for an import ([docs/MIGRATION.md](MIGRATION.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `SM_MIGRATION_MAX_UNPACKED_MB`        | `20480`      | Most a migration package may unpack to (tables, files, audit log); the import also checks for free disk space first ([docs/MIGRATION.md](MIGRATION.md))                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SM_TRANSFER_PASSPHRASE`              | –            | Transfer passphrase for `steward migrate` (automation only; prefer `--transfer-passphrase-file` or the prompt). Or `SM_TRANSFER_PASSPHRASE_FILE`                                                                                                                                                                                         |
